snippets.title: Low heater output at idle from auxiliary coolant pump
snippets.text: Applies to 2.4L I4 engines, model years 2021-2023, with an electric auxiliary coolant pump. Heater output may drop at idle in cold weather when the auxiliary pump does not run. Command the pump on with a scan tool and listen for operation at the pump. Repair: replace the auxiliary coolant pump.

snippets.title: No heat from rear auxiliary heater
snippets.text: Applies to minivans with rear auxiliary heat, model years 2011-2019. The front heater works normally but the rear vents blow cool because the rear heater control valve sticks closed. Command the rear heat on and feel both rear heater hoses under the vehicle. Repair: replace the rear heater control valve.

snippets.title: Passenger side cold on dual-zone climate control
snippets.text: Applies to all models with dual-zone automatic climate control. Heat may be normal on the driver side while the passenger side blows cool, caused by the passenger blend door actuator losing its calibration. Run the climate control self-test and read stored HVAC codes. Repair: recalibrate or replace the passenger blend door actuator.

snippets.title: No crank from clutch pedal position switch
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a manual transmission. The starter may not engage when the clutch pedal switch does not close fully with the pedal pressed. Check switch continuity with the pedal fully depressed. Repair: adjust or replace the clutch pedal position switch.

snippets.title: Starter control circuit check
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Back-probe the starter solenoid S terminal and have a helper attempt a start in park. The S terminal should receive at least 10.5 V during the attempt. Low or no voltage points to the control side (relay, range switch or wiring) rather than the starter itself.

snippets.title: Battery voltage during a start attempt
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Connect a meter across the battery posts and watch the reading while a helper attempts to start the engine. Voltage should not fall below 9.6 V. A battery that collapses below that value cannot power the starter even if dash lights look bright with the key on.

snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. With the engine off, pump the brake pedal several times to use up booster reserve. Apply steady, moderate pressure to the pedal and hold it for one minute. A pedal that slowly sinks toward the floor with no external leak indicates fluid bypassing inside the master cylinder.

snippets.title: Brake temperature comparison
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. After a test drive with several moderate stops, park without using the parking brake and measure each front rotor face with an infrared thermometer. Temperatures should be within about 50 deg F side to side. A large difference shows which side is braking harder or dragging.

snippets.title: Brake hose restriction test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. With the front wheels off the ground, have a helper press and release the brake pedal firmly. Immediately spin each front wheel by hand. Both wheels should turn freely right after release. A wheel that stays dragged for several moments indicates a hose that is restricting fluid return.
